summary: Verification of the FEEDBACK review's fix wave on the merged head: is each finding the wave took actually fixed, judged from fresh recordings, and did the wave break anything (the hurt cue's bearing and its new acts; the boss roof gap, the 41 InsetBlocks and the calmer mirrored ground; the Thug, Kicker, Ox, Bruiser and Punk at 1 m)
read_first: docs/reviews/M6/findings-feedback.json: the review's 18 findings in full (detail, evidence, repro, suggested fix, skeptic votes); the ids your lens verifies are named in your brief
docs/reviews/M6/fix-feedback-final.md: what the fix wave was asked to do, per package, and 'Done when'
docs/milestones/M6-calls/FIX-FEEL.md, FIX-WORLD.md, FIX-ART-A.md, FIX-ART-B.md: what each fixer says it did, its numbers and its judgement calls (claims to check, not facts)

lenses.brief: VERIFY the art findings the fix wave took, then hunt for what it broke. The findings: feedback-chars-01 (the Thug's black half-face), -02 (his chest valley scribble), -03 (Ox's grey face blotches taking cloth damage), -04 (the Kicker's black eye bar), -05 (his mask slashes), -06 (the Bruiser's striped visor and cream wedge), -07 (his purple helmet bleeding), -08 (the Thug's dashed waistband), and the Punk's scribbly vest valleys from the review's common note. For each, say fixed, partly fixed or not fixed, with the still that shows it: BEFORE is /Users/arachne/repos/beat-em-up-PoC/captures/m6-feedback-review/<slug>/ (the review round's recordings on 82bab12), AFTER is captures_dir/<slug>/ (the same acts on the merged head d582d21): r_kicker, r_thug, r_bruiser, r_boss (each 'Look: <label> at 1 m'), dt, dk, dj, dox, dp1 (each turned 0, 90 and 150 degrees at 1.6 m), lineup, heavies (2.5, 5 and 10 m), damage ('Look: tune damage at 1 m'), fight ('Mixed six, fight', the roster moving). The fixers' own before/after sheets are in /Users/arachne/repos/beat-em-up-PoC/.worktrees/m6-fix-art-a/captures/ and .worktrees/m6-fix-art-b/captures/sheets/ (read them only to see what they claimed). Check these claims hard: (a) FIX-ART-B says Ox's remaining mauve face patches are the toon shadow band on smoothed normals, not a palette slot, so the finding is 'answered, not fixed'; confirm or refute it (look_texel_swatch off against on, the damage act: do those patches still take cloth damage?); (b) the Kicker's eyes are now a bare skin band under the cap with no drawn feature; judge it against his concept (assets/source/concepts/m6/kicker_c.jpg) at 1 m and 2.5 m: closer or further than M6's look; (c) Ox's new nose stroke is 'a little heavy': is it a blot at 1 m; (d) the Thug's new hood_neck and waist zones: is the drape and pocket ink the concept draws still there; (e) the Bruiser's new helmet slot 47: does the helmet still match his jacket purple at 1, 2.5 and 5 m, and in the damage act does it scuff without blood while his face still bleeds; (f) the Punk's calmer vest (min_chain_m 0.45 -> 0.6, a bigger move than the brief's 0.55): are pockets and hem still inked, and is the veteran still clearly different at 5 m (lineup). Then REGRESSIONS: anything on any of the five that is worse than the BEFORE stills, at any distance, and any crawl or shimmer in motion (fight) that the BEFORE fight did not have. Out of scope (left by the lead, don't report): the Punk's cap logo blot, the Bruiser's cuff ovals, Ox's sawtooth sleeve. Each finding names the character, the distance, the before and after stills, and the config key or file that fixes it (assets/source/characters/<id>/pipeline.json; assets/source/palette/<id>.json).

VERIFY the world and feel findings the fix wave took, then hunt for what it broke. HURT FEEL: feedback-world-01 (the hurt cue's bearing was near random) and -03 (no recording of a finisher, a block or a burst). Source: captures_dir/hurt ('Look: player hurt' and its three new acts: a Punk jab and a Bruiser smash from the front, left, right and behind; finishers (a synthetic FINISHER-tier hit, logged 'synthetic', because no enemy move is FINISHER tier); blocked hits; a burst of three Punks), and the REAL hits in passive_mix ('Bruiser among Punks, passive') and passive_six ('Six Punks, passive'): no god mode, the player stands passive among the real AI for 25 s and takes 26-30 damaging hits from every side (Punk jab, cross and shove, Bruiser smash and headbutt); each hit is a bot.log line 'f<frame> Player: <move> <dmg> dmg <tier>' (the frame is the movie frame at 60 fps), and the WARN lines give the rear warning's bearings. run_street and fight have almost no clean damaging hits (the held-back pilot parries them; fight runs in god mode at 0 damage), so judge real play from the two passive acts; there is no BEFORE of them. Check for every hit you can find: the ink strokes sit on the edge the attacker stands on (front = top, behind = bottom), the head rolls away from the blow, the cue is unmistakable at the moment it lands, the burst is not nauseating, the bottom strokes are not hidden by the HP panel, blocked hits stay as light as M6. In the passive recordings, use bot.log to find when the player is hit and by whom, cut frames there with ffmpeg, and check the edge against where that enemy stands in the frame (or off it). The BEFORE is /Users/arachne/repos/beat-em-up-PoC/captures/m6-feedback-review/hurt and run_street. GROUND AND GEOMETRY: feedback-world-02 and -code-02 (the boss roof gap z-fight with the skyline strips), -world-05 (a camouflage-like, darker ground with a visible 8 m repeat), -code-03 (strip ink fading early on grazing surfaces). Sources: drift ('Look: ground drift', now ending with held views of the boss roof gap, the deck and the far deck; measure with python3 -I tools/ground_flicker.py <avi> [log]), tour ('Look: arena tour', every arena), walk ('Perf: level walk', god mode through the whole level, the act of Game-boy's flashing report), run_street. Check: (1) nothing flashes, toggles or swims anywhere a player walks or looks, the boss roof gap included; (2) the ground reads as a comic ground closer to assets/source/concepts/m6/mood_street_a.jpg than the BEFORE (captures/m6-feedback-review/drift, tour, walk), the 16 m mirrored repeat is not obvious, and the A1 drift numbers that rose (still 0.0165 -> 0.0291, creep 0.094 -> 0.117, walk 0.574 -> 1.118) are invisible in play; (3) THE 41 INSETBLOCKS: FIX-WORLD pulled the drawn mesh of 41 blocks in street.tscn, roofs.tscn and boss_roof.tscn 2 cm inside their colliders and looked only at the gap, the deck and street A1/A2. Look at the rest: wall tops, corners, kerbs, doorways, drop edges, roof parapets, every arena in the tour and walk, for a crack, a sliver of sky or void, a light leak, a floating or sunken edge, a seam line, or a visible step where a recessed face meets a neighbouring block; (4) the ground's mirror: a visible seam, a mip line or a hard edge at the 8 m boundaries where the tile flips. Each finding names the act, the time or still, and the file or tunable that fixes it.

Code, tests and ledgers over the fix wave's diff: git diff 2afbe4d d582d21 (2afbe4d is the head before the wave; the four merges are m6/fix-feel, m6/fix-world, m6/fix-art-a, m6/fix-art-b). VERIFY feedback-code-01 and -world-04 (the hurt shape numbers as tunables), -code-02 (the general coplanar guard), -code-03 (the strip fade footprint), -code-04 (ASSETS rows), -code-05 (the vacuous guards), and the code side of -world-01. Check: FirstPersonCamera.hit_bearing reads the attacker's position read-only, handles an attacker that is null, freed (is_instance_valid), not in the tree or within hurt_bearing_min_m of the lens, and the overlay and the roll take the same bearing; the six real-hit tests can fail (put the old contact-point bearing back in a scratch copy and run them; FIX-FEEL says five fail); the 15 new tunables are @export_range in a 'Hit feel > Hurt' group with the old literals as defaults, tuning/default.json matches `godot --headless -s tools/gen_default_preset.gd`, and no feel number is left as a literal in game/ui/hurt_overlay.gd, game/ui/player_health_panel.gd or the camera's hurt path; the layer rules (the overlay, the camera and the panel only read state); InsetBlock (game/level/kit/inset_block.gd): the collider is exactly the parent's (tests/test_m6_colliders.gd passes and covers the 41), the inset is right on every axis and both faces for each tier, INSET_STEP_M as a constant against the 'no numbers in scripts' rule; tests/m6_coplanar_scan.gd: can it fail (move BossRoof Ground's top back to 0 or -0.5 in a scratch copy and run tests/test_m6_feedback_ground.gd), what its exclusions (covered by a third box, facing no floor, under 0.02 m2, the rooms at 0.5 m2) could hide; game/fx/trim_body.gdshaderinc: the mirrored ground's UV and derivatives at the 8 m tile flips (a fract/mirror with discontinuous derivatives draws a one-pixel mip seam; check how the gradients are taken), and the sqrt(|det|) strip fade; tools/gen_trim.gd (`godot --headless -s tools/gen_trim.gd -- --check` says the sheet matches); the art configs: every run.py --check (bruiser, boss, kicker, thug, punk, dummy) and gen_palette.py --check reproducible; palette regions with only_from match the calls files; slot 47 bruiser_helmet has blood false and the same colour as slot 44; _rolled_out(id) now needs detail_bake.crease and the new test that each roll-out test names its own pipeline.json can fail; tests/fixtures/strain/bruiser.json was regenerated by FIX-ART-B (the held clip's min went 0.1489 -> 0.088): find why a palette-only change moved mesh strain, whether the loosening is logged with its reason in the roster and calls files, and whether it is no looser than needed; the Punk's min_chain_m moved 0.45 -> 0.6 where the brief said 0.55; ASSETS.md rows for every changed binary (thug, kicker, boss, bruiser and punk GLBs and detail masks, palette_atlas.png, punk_veteran_atlas.png, ground_sheet.png); no key printed or written; no Tripo, Gemini or ElevenLabs spend. The merged suite is already run (below): don't rerun the whole suite; run single files with -gselect where you need them.

common_note: State: m6/full-art-audio at d582d21, PR #6 open and unmerged. The FEEDBACK round's nine packages (82bab12) were reviewed (docs/reviews/M6/findings-feedback.json: 2 highs and 5 mediums survived, plus lows the lead took), and a fix wave of four Sonnet fixers (FIX-FEEL, FIX-WORLD, FIX-ART-A, FIX-ART-B; calls in docs/milestones/M6-calls/FIX-*.md) was merged at d582d21. This round checks that wave independently: you did not build it, and its fixers' claims are claims. Suite on the merged head: 2027/2027 in 414 s with ART_PUNK_VARIANT_STRAIN=1, 0 SCRIPT/SHADER/ERROR lines, the same 3 expected warnings as before. Every run.py --check, player_run.py --asset player --check, gen_palette.py --check and gen_trim.gd --check said YES after the merge. The lead's look at the fixers' stills: the hurt edges match the side for the Bruiser smash from four sides; the ground is calmer and paler; the Thug's half-face is gone; the Bruiser's cream wedge is gone; Ox gained nose, mouth and jaw strokes; the Kicker's eyes became a plain skin band (less like shades). Fresh recordings on d582d21 are in captures_dir, one folder per act (bot.avi, bot.log, sheets/; look acts have per-mark stills): r_kicker, r_thug, r_bruiser, r_boss, lineup, heavies, dj, dk, dt, dp1, dox, damage, hurt, fight (crowd bot); passive_mix, passive_six (crowd bot, no god mode, the player passive and taking real hits); drift, tour, walk, run_street (level bots on mission1.tscn). Frame time (the lead's, not a finding): the fixed head is -0.6% against the build Game-boy played. The same acts on 82bab12 (the BEFORE) are in /Users/arachne/repos/beat-em-up-PoC/captures/m6-feedback-review/. Cut finer stills with ffmpeg from bot.avi when you need a moment. Severity: high = Game-boy would see it in normal play and it undoes one of his four asks (the ground flashing, the GO sting, not feeling hits, blobby enemies); medium = visible at 1-3 m or in a fight, or a rule or test that does not hold; low = everything else. A finding the wave was asked to fix and did not fix is at least the severity it had. Perf is the lead's (measured separately), not a finding. Spec departures already ruled by Game-boy: the victim camera stack and the silent GO (README).
